newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mostly lower after G7 meeting.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mostly lower after G7 meeting.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mostly lower after G7 officials failed to add specifics to their foreign exchange policy after Sunday's meeting, traders and analysts said.
The G7 reiterated they would intervene when appropriate but did specify the levels that they consider appropriate.
"No one knows what the appropriate levels are," one currency trader said.
One senior Japanese finance ministry official said Japanese and U.S. statements were deliberately vague because specific references could have caused "unnecessary market reaction."

However, June marks set a contract low of $0.5768 on GLOBEX, below the previous contract low of $0.5780, while June yen held above the contract low of $0.007936 overnight. The dollar/yen attempted, but failed, to test the 4-1/3-year high of about 127.16 spot.
"I would have really thought we'd test 126.89 spot by now," one currency futures trader said. The 126.89 spot level corresponds to the June yen contract low of $0.007936.
"But we have sickeningly tight ranges," he said.
He said estimated volume in the first hour of trade was at 2,700 in yen, and 3,000 in marks and 1,600 in Swiss francs.
Another trader said the G7 communique was not the green light dollar bulls were anticipating ahead of Sunday's meeting.
"It was a symmetrical communique," he said. "You could make equal arguments for dollar strength and dollar weakness."
He and other traders noted underlying concerns that Japan may raise Japanese interest rates in the near- to intermediate-term.
The yield on the 10-year Japanese government bonds continued to edge higher from last week.
Also, separate comments from G7 officials also reflected the split market sentiment about the communique.

Bank of England governor Eddie George said G7 officials felt the exchange rate environment was in "pretty good shape," and no need had been expressed for an action plan to deal with any future currency moves.
Meanwhile, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he "can't do along with" forecasts that the mark could fall to a yearly average of 1.80 to the dollar, or $0.5575 in June marks.
Tietmeyer also said he saw no need for a change in German interst rates, and said forex rates are reflecting economic fundamentals.

At 0849 CDT/1349 GMT, June yen was off $0.000024 at $0.007952, marks were off $0.0011 at $0.5801, Swiss francs were off $0.0014 at $0.6830, sterling were $0.0004 at $1.6214, Canadian dollars were down $0.0011 at $0.7173, Australian dollars were $0.0037 higher at $0.7805 and Mexican pesos were $0.000275 at $0.123500. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
